**Title (English, from literature):** Tickling

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 52 (*Aṅgulipatodaka*) is a disciplinary rule in the *Vinaya Piṭaka* governing the conduct of Buddhist monks. The rule stipulates that a monk who tickles another monk commits an offense requiring expiation (*pācittiya*) and must confess it. In modern scholarship and translations, the text has been rendered into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali. None of the secondary literature passages retrieved in the research dossier discuss this rule; instead, they address the homonymous Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 52 concerning verbal abuse of monks.

 A counterpart rule for nuns also exists in the Pali *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Pācittiya 133) and across the corresponding non-Theravāda nuns' codes.

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog data.*
